mined.title: Kukkiwon International Master Course, History of Taekwondo / Grandmaster Jun Lee 9th Dan

passages.text: Silla Hwarang: horseback riding, sword, archery and moral training; why Korean martial arts stress ethics and filial piety (Hwarang rules).
Tang Soo Do / Kong Soo Do: the same characters are read karate in Japanese; Korean schools used these names for Korean karate before 1955.

Naming story: President Rhee sees an army demonstration, calls it taekkyon; Choi's naming committee keeps tae (foot) and replaces the hand character with kwon (fist); name proclaimed April 1955; KTA from 1959.
1961: Tae Soo Do compromise name (part karate, part taekwondo) for the association, until the 1965 return to Taekwondo.
1972 Kukkiwon completed, 1973 named; first World Championships hosted by Kukkiwon in 1973.

mined.caveat: Presenter's personal telling of history; auto-captions garble Korean names (e.g. 'cookie one' for Kukkiwon). Dates agree with Wikipedia except KTA 1959 vs 1961 (see REPORT).

mined.title: Ep. 34 - KUKKIWON - The Unseen force behind global Taekwondo rise (english)

passages.text: Construction began 19 Nov 1971, main structure done 30 Nov 1972, official name Kukkiwon 6 Feb 1973; blue roof tiles like the presidential residence.
First World Championships 25 May 1973; first Dan certificates issued 9 Dec 1973 so that a dan means the same in Seoul or Berlin.
From 1 Mar 1980 Kukkiwon handles all Poom/Dan exams and certificates; World Taekwondo Academy trains instructors; IOC President Samaranch visited 8 Apr 1982.
First Taekwondo Hanmadang 9 Dec 1992 (festival, distinct from sparring tournaments).
Only a Kukkiwon-confirmed black belt (Poom/Dan) may compete in official WT events including the Olympics.

mined.caveat: Summary-style generated discussion of Kukkiwon's own timeline; dates cross-checked against de/en/ko Wikipedia (construction, naming, 1973 championship all match).

mined.title: Historia del Taekwondo (English-narrated Korean documentary)
mined.language: en (auto-captions of the English narration; title in Spanish)

passages.text: Goguryeo tomb murals show bare-fist fighting; Goguryeo's 'sunbae' warrior system; Silla Hwarang and Buddhism as the base of the martial tradition (official-narrative origin story).
After 1945 karate training was introduced; hand-heavy fighting was called tangsudo/kongsudo; efforts to restore traditional arts (taekkyon masters) prepared modern taekwondo.
Basic punch: the fist travels straight while the wrist rotates at the end, like rifling in a gun barrel; defence uses waist rotation.
Why taekwondo kicks fold the knee first and use the joint like a flail (speed, hidden intent), unlike straight-leg Chinese kicks; defence and offence often happen together.

mined.caveat: Promotional documentary, strongly traditionalist (indigenous-origin) framing; useful for 'why' explanations of kicks and punches, weaker as history.

mined.title: 2024 Taekwondo Poomsae Rule Update

passages.text: 0.3 accuracy deduction for finishing a foot away from the start point was deleted for recognised poomsae.
Examples of 0.3 accuracy deductions (e.g. eyes closed, wrong gaze while kicking) and 0.1 deductions (e.g. fist shape for support).

Freestyle poomsae technical scoring changed: base score 0.1-0.7 plus additional score; jumping side kick counts only if supporting leg does not touch the kicking leg; additional 0.1/0.2/0.3 for 1/2/3+ kick types; 360/540/720+ turning kicks give 0.1/0.2/0.3.

mined.caveat: WT competition rules as of 14 June 2024, not Kukkiwon curriculum content; a presenter's reading of the rules, so confirm against the WT rulebook before using.
